gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same false inference: liminf convergence of the objective, or convergence of its running minimum, does not imply monotone convergence of the raw objective sequence. It also gives the corresponding running-minimum repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem incorrectly promotes a liminf/best-iterate guarantee to monotone full-sequence convergence of the raw objective values, despite the method not being a descent method.

component_coverage.gold_component: The raw sequence kappa(cDo(d_k)) is incorrectly claimed to decrease monotonically and converge; only the liminf or running-best sequence is justified.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes the valid liminf/running-minimum conclusion from the unsupported monotone convergence claim for the raw objective and supplies the corrected statement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns the nonsmooth necessity direction of an eigenvector characterization for optimal diagonal preconditioning and the need for convex combinations in extreme eigenspaces. Gold issue I004 instead concerns the orientation and optimality of a triangular Cholesky right factor B_i in a block-scaled objective. The prediction does not diagnose that factor-orientation error.
